en: The Sūtra on the Eight Auspicious Divine Spells Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Yuezhi during the Wu Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in Rājagṛha, together with a thousand [monks].
Accompanied by two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, and with a thousand bodhisattvas all of whom were like Maitreya,
the Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra and the bhikṣus: “All of you,
listen with single-minded attention!”
The Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra:

"To the east, at a distance of one *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands], there is a Buddha named King of Peaceful Entrustment, Fully Endowed (*An-yin-zhul-lè-mǎn-jùzú-wáng* Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha), who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma. His world is named Assembly of Fulfilled Wishes (*Mǎnsuòyuàn-jù*).”

"Two *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* beyond here, there is a Buddha named King Endowed with Lapis Lazuli, a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Radiance of Compassion."

"Three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* beyond here, there is a Buddha named Saṃcodana-sarvakuśalamūla-paripūrṇa-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Nandī-sukha."

“Four times the sands of the Ganges away from here, there is a Buddha named Aśokaguṇasampannarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Sarvasukhāvatīpraveśa.”

“Five *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands] away from here, there is a Buddha named Bhaiṣajyarāja-saṃpūrṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Sarvaratnadharmapūrṇa.”

"Six *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands] away from here, there is a Buddha named Padmavyūharāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Pūrṇagandhayaśas."

"Seven *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands] away from here, there is a Buddha named Gaṇanā-saṃkhyā-samavasaraṇa-sampanna-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma. His world is named Sarva-vyākhyāna-śabda-dūra-śruta."

“Eight *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands] away from here, there is a Buddha named Sarvabandhanavimocanasampannarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Sarvavimukti.”
The Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra:

“These Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who have transcended the four paths and do not undergo further rebirth, possess pure lands that are free from the five turbidities, devoid of sensual desire, and without mental defilements.”

If there are good sons or good daughters who, upon hearing the names of these eight Buddhas and their lands, receive, uphold, practice, and recite them, and extensively explain their meaning to others, they shall never be foolish; whatever they speak shall be free from error; they shall be fully endowed with the primary and secondary marks of a Buddha, without any deficiency, and for countless years they shall never lack anything.

"This person shall never fall into the hells of the Great Mountain, nor among the hungry ghosts or animals; this person shall never aspire to attain the path of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha and enter parinirvāṇa, but shall surely attain the unsurpassed path of equality, constantly encounter dhāraṇīs, always practice the bodhisattva path, and obtain immeasurable merit."

"The Four Great Heavenly Kings will constantly protect them; they shall not be arrested by government officials, nor harmed by thieves or robbers, nor disturbed by devas, nāgas, or spirits. Yakṣas, ghost-spirits, spirits of sorcery, whether human or non-human—none shall be able to injure, kill, or find an opportunity against them, except for those consequences resulting from their own past karma."

"If one suffers from illness, water or fire disasters, the cawing of crows, evil dreams, or the harassment of various demons, and when experiencing such terrors that the hair on one's body stands on end, one should constantly read this *Bhadraṣṭāṅga-guhyadhāraṇī-sūtra* to recite its spells; then one will immediately obtain healing and recovery."
At that time, the Buddha spoke these verses:
"If there are those who uphold this sutra, The names of the eight buddha-lands shall be theirs;
They shall not fall into the three evil realms, And shall swiftly attain the unsurpassed path."
Having personally awakened to the aspiration for the Way, upon seeing the Buddha, they immediately attained understanding;
with constant joy within and without, they made offerings with a reverent heart.
For billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, all their evil deeds were completely eliminated.
By upholding these eight auspicious verses, one will swiftly attain clear understanding of the teachings.
Those who serve this sutra shall be born within a thousand-petaled lotus;
from it shall emerge precious jewels, and their physical form and appearance will be unsurpassed in excellence.
Those who hear this honored sutra and respect, believe in, and delight in it,
upholding, reciting, and reading it with purity and without negligence;
those women who believe in this sutra will be reverent, cautious, and free from flattery.
A woman who abandons her female form becomes a man, always intelligent and sagacious;
by upholding the names of these eight Buddhas, she shall not be harmed by thieves as she goes in or out.
Neither weapons, nor water, nor fire, nor poison—none of these malevolent things can affect her.
Those who love and delight in upholding this sutra will find no opportunity for Māras to gain the upper hand.
Neither ghosts, spirits, nor their various subordinates shall be able to disturb them.
They shall fly to all Buddha-fields, wherever they go, there shall be great abundance and joy.
With a mind upright and free from evil, seeing the Buddha brings great joy;
wherever one is born, one always encounters a Buddha and serves them with an impartial heart.
All evils are eliminated, and one swiftly attains the path of Nirvāṇa.
Exerting diligence without indolence, they depart from all conditions and attachments.
Being simple, upright, and scholarly, they uphold the names of the eight Buddhas;
with valor they subdue the hosts of Māras, their power like that of a vajra.
Endowed with the marks of physical perfection, none can withstand him;
Free from stinginess in his giving, he is reborn into a household of hundreds of millions.
Thieves and enemies alike are naturally and entirely eliminated.
Regarding illnesses, matters of state officials, the cawing of crows, and various evil dreams—
if one holds these names of the eight Buddhas and recites them as a mantra, they will be immediately eliminated and healed.
Those who uphold this sutra [shall be protected by] Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others.
The first four Heavenly Kings will always protect them together.
All their aspirations shall be fulfilled; they leap for joy with great delight.
For those who believe and rejoice with a single mind, their merit shall be just like this.

At that time, there were eight bodhisattvas—Bhadrapāla Bodhisattva, Ratnākara Bodhisattva, Gayākāśyapa Bodhisattva, Naradatta Bodhisattva, Susīma Bodhisattva, Mahāsusārthavāha Bodhisattva, Aṅgiras Bodhisattva, and Varuṇadeva Bodhisattva—who had sought the Way for incalculable kalpas and had not yet attained Buddhahood. They made this vow:
"May all the people of the world throughout the ten directions attain the Buddha-way."
If anyone suffers from a sudden illness, they should call upon the names of us eight; they shall immediately attain liberation.
When their life is about to end, we eight shall fly there to welcome and escort them.
The various bodhisattvas, Maitreya and others, as well as the four foremost kings of the devas, all addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We shall protect those who uphold this *Sūtra of the Eight Auspicious Divine Mantras*; together with us, we shall exert our strength to ensure that all illnesses are completely cured."

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Śāriputra, Maitreya Bodhisattva, as well as all the bhikṣus, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and asura kings, were all greatly rejoiced and delighted to hear it.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Eight Auspicious Divine Mantras.
